item.title: Urban street trees lose much of their capacity to cool during droughts
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: The combination of heat waves and drought markedly reduces the capacity of street trees to cool the air in Mediterranean cities. The lack of soil moisture severely restricts plant transpiration, reducing the thermal relief provided by these trees during extreme heat events.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: treat the method as a way to see structure, heat, or vegetation stress — not a spectacle. item.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.
Waypoint’s Take: Outside, this matters because it can change what you watch for: compare forecast cues with what the sky, wind, and ground feel like before you commit to a route.
